questions.question: The Parliamentary form of government is also referred to as the ______ model.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Westminster.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Westminster model refers to the system of government in which the executive branch (prime minister and cabinet) is accountable to the legislature (parliament).**
 
• This model originated in the** United Kingdom** and has been adopted by many other countries, including India, Canada, and Australia.
 
• The term **"parliamentary" is used because the legislature plays a central role in the government**, with members elected by the people and responsible for making laws and holding the executive accountable.
 
• Other features of the **Westminster model include a strong two-party system**, a focus on the rule of law and individual rights, and a tradition of civil service neutrality and expertise.
 
• The Parliamentary System of government in India is taken from the British(UK)​constitution.
 
• The parliamentary system of government(PSA): 
 
 
• PSA means that the executive government branch of has the indirect or direct support of the parliament.
 
• This direct or indirect support is generally shown by a vote of confidence.
 
• The relationship between the legislature and the executive branch in any parliamentary system is called responsible government.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theocracy** refers to a government **ruled by religious leaders, **which is not a form of parliamentary government.
 
• **Plutocracy** refers to a government ruled by the **wealthy,** which is not a form of government at all but rather a social system.
 
• **Communism** refers to a system of government in which p**roperty and resources are owned collectively by the people,** which is not a form of parliamentary government but rather a type of socialism.

questions.question: El Nino is a phenomenon in which a warm ocean current that flows past the _______ coast, in place of the cold current, every 2 to 5 years.
questions.solution:

• Trade winds and the atmosphere are also impacted by El Niño. 
 
• El Niño is a climate pattern that describes the unusual warming of surface waters in the eastern tropical Pacific Ocean.
 
• **El Nino, meaning "Child Christ'**' is a warm ocean current appearing along the Peru coast, generally in December. 
 
• It normally happens once every 4-5 years though it is not fixed. 
 
• It replaces the cold Peru Ocean current flowing along the Peru coast in normal years.

questions.question: In India, which programme provides food grains and other essential commodities at subsidised prices in rural and urban areas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the__** Public Distribution System.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gramdan is a concept that was introduced by Vinoba Bhave, which means the donation of land for the common good. **

 
 
• **It is not a programme that provides food grains or essential commodities.**
 
 
 
• ** Buffer Stock** refers to the stock of food grains that is maintained by the **government to stabilise prices and ensure food security.** It is not a programme that provides food grains or essential commodities directly to the people.
 
• Bhoodan is also a concept introduced by Vinoba Bhave, which means the donation of land by landlords to landless farmers.
 
 
• It is not a programme that provides food grains or essential commodities.

** Public Distribution System:**

 
• **The PDS was introduced in India in 1947** to provide food security to the poor and to stabilise prices.
 
• **The PDS distributes essential commodities** such as rice, wheat, sugar, and kerosene at subsidised prices through a network of Fair Price Shops (FPS) across the country.
 
• The PDS is implemented by the **Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution and is one of the largest food security programmes in the world.**
 
• The PDS has undergone several reforms in recent years, including the introduction of** Aadhaar-based biometric authentication to prevent leakages and ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.**

questions.question: Loans create ________, as they have to be returned to the lender in a certain period of time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**liability.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loans are a liability because they represent an obligation that has to be fulfilled by the borrower.**
 
• When a loan is taken, **the borrower receives funds that are recorded as a liability on the balance sheet, which needs to be repaid with interest within a specific period.**
 
• **The repayment of loans** is a crucial aspect of financial management as it affects a company's cash flow and the ability to take on new debt or invest in growth opportunities.
 
• **Assets **are anything that a company owns that has value, such as equipment, inventory, or property. Equity represents the residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting liabilities. Growth is the increase in the value of assets or the expansion of a business.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asset: **An asset is anything that a company owns that has value and can be converted into cash.

 
 
• Examples of assets include equipment, inventory, property, and investments. Assets are typically recorded on the balance sheet and can be categorized as current or non-current.
 
 
 
• **Growth:** Growth refers to the increase in the value of assets or the expansion of a business.
 
 
• It can be measured in terms of revenue, profits, market share, or other key performance indicators. Growth is essential for businesses to remain competitive and achieve long-term success.
 
 
 
• **Equity:** Equity represents the residual interest in the assets of an entity after deducting liabilities.
 
 
• It can be thought of as the net worth of a company, and it is calculated by subtracting liabilities from assets. Equity can be divided into two main categories: owner's equity and retained earnings.
 
• Owner's equity represents the investment made by the owners, while retained earnings are the profits that have been reinvested into the company.
 
 
 
• ** Liability:** A liability is an obligation that a company owes to another party, such as a loan or debt. Liabilities are recorded on the balance sheet and can be classified as current or non-current.
 
 
• Current liabilities are due within one year, while non-current liabilities are due after one year.
 
• Liabilities are a crucial aspect of financial management as they impact a company's cash flow and ability to take on new debt or invest in growth opportunities.

questions.question: Which of the following was the main argument put forward by the British for the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal (1905), was carried out by the British Viceroy in India, Lord Curzon.**
 
• The partition was supported by the Muslims of East Bengal and their support was motivated by the poor economic conditions in East Bengal.
 
• The decision to **split Bengal came in July and by October 16, 1905**, Bengal had been divided into Piston Bengal and Assam and the rest of Bengal.
 
• The partition separated the largely Muslim eastern areas from the largely Hindu western areas.
 
• Administrative Convenience was given an official reason by the Britishers for the partition of Bengal in 1905.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Facts about the partition of Bengal are:**

 
 
• The provincial state of Bengal had a population of nearly 80 million at that time.
 
• It included the Hindi-speaking regions of Bihar, the Odia-speaking regions of Odisha, and the Assamese-speaking region of Assam.
 
• The government announced the idea for partition in January 1904.
 
• The idea was opposed by Henry John Stedman Cotton, Chief Commissioner of Assam.
 
• But the Partition of Bengal went on to happen on October 16, 1905, by Viceroy Curzon.
 
 

 
• **Annulment of Bengal**

 
 
• The partition of Bengal was** annulled in 1911**.
 
• Partition of Bengal was canceled by Lord Hardinge II.
 
• The c**apital of British India was moved to Delhi from Calcutta in 1911.**

questions.question: Which gas is released on burning of natural gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Carbon dioxide.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **The gas released by burning natural gas is carbon dioxide (CO2).**
 
• Natural gas mainly consists of methane (CH4) which is a hydrocarbon.
 
• When it is burned, it reacts with oxygen (O2) in the air and produces carbon dioxide and water vapor.
 
• The process of combustion is a process in which the material reacts with oxygen dioxide, releasing energy in the form of light and heat.
 
 
• Combustion reactions must require O₂ as a single reactant. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide **is a greenhouse gas and its emission contributes to **global warming and climate change.**
 
• **Hydrogen (H₂)** is not released on **burning natural gas.** However, it can be produced by steam reforming of natural gas.
 
• **Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S)** is a colorless gas with a** foul odor. **It is sometimes present in natural gas and can cause corrosion in pipes and equipment. It is removed during the processing of natural gas.
 
• ** Ozone (O₃) **is not released by burning natural gas. It is a form of oxygen that is formed by the action of sunlight on pollutants such as** nitrogen oxides (NOx) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs).**

questions.question: Janaki Prasad is associated with which Gharana of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Banaras gharana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Janaki Prasad is associated with the Banaras Gharana of Kathak, which is known for its intricate footwork and graceful movements.**

 
 
• This gharana originated in the **city of Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh** and is characterized by its emphasis on layakari (rhythmic play) tandava (masculine) and lasya (feminine) elements.
 
• The Banaras Gharana is known for its** intricate footwork and graceful movements**.
 
 
 
• The Lucknow Gharana, also known as the Purrab Gharana, is one of the oldest and most influential schools of Kathak. It is known for its graceful, delicate movements and intricate footwork.
 
• The Jaipur Gharana, also known as the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, is known for its emphasis on technical precision and rhythmic complexity.
 
• The Raigarh Gharana, also known as the Kalka-Bindadin Gharana, is a relatively new school of Kathak that emerged in the early 20th century in the town of Raigarh in Chhattisgarh. It is known for its use of acrobatic movements and martial arts-inspired techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​The 'UP Sangeet Natak Akademi' was established on 13 November 1963.
 
• 'Kathak dance' is the Shastri dance of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Kathak is the dance form of Rajasthan and North India.
 
• In the medieval period, it was related to Krishna Katha and dance.
 
• At present, Birju Maharaj has been its great lecturer.

questions.question: What comes at the top of the food guide pyramid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** fats and sugars.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The food guide pyramid is a visual representation of the recommended amounts of different food groups that should be consumed in a healthy diet.**
 
• **Cereal grains,** are located in the** second tier** of the pyramid and should be** consumed in moderate amounts.**
 
• **Fruits and vegetables,** are located in the **third tier** of the pyramid and should be consumed in** larger amounts than grains and fats/sugars.**
 
• **Pulses and legumes**, are also located in the **third tier** of the pyramid and should be consumed in moderate amounts as they provide protein and other important nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Food Chain- **

 
• It is defined as the transfer of food energy from green plants (producers) through a series of organisms with repeated eating and then being eaten.
 
• Any food chain in our nature essentially starts with producers and ends with animals or top carnivores.
 
• There are 2 types of food chains namely- Grazing Food Chain and Detritus Food Chain.

**Food Pyramids-**

 
• If the trophic levels of any food chain are drawn vertically then it is said to be an **Ecological Pyramid.**
 
• There are 3 types of Pyramids for every Ecosystem namely- **Numbers Pyramid, Energy Pyramid, and Biomass Pyramid.**
 
• The Autotrophs form the base of the pyramid while the Top Carnivores from the tip of the Pyramid.
